\chapter{Greetings People Actually Say}
\label{ch:ka-greetings-people-say}
\hlchaptermodality{96}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can greet someone the way Kannada speakers do day to day: have you eaten, what's new, long time, hello, are you well.}

\section[ūṭa āytā]{\kn{ಊಟ} \kn{ಆಯ್ತಾ} (ūṭa āytā) — have you eaten?}

\label{lesson:KA-C96-eaten}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for maybe, then the Kannada for certainly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಊಟ} \kn{ಆಯ್ತಾ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಊಟ} \kn{ಆಯ್ತಾ}?} (\emph{ūṭa āytā?}) — \textquotedblleft{}have you eaten?\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}has the meal happened?\textquotedblright{}. In the south this is a greeting as much as a question.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The warmest everyday hello.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ūṭa āytā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ūṭa āytā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{ūṭa āytā?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for maybe, then the Kannada for certainly, then say \emph{ūṭa āytā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಊಟ} \kn{ಆಯ್ತಾ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Have you eaten?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ēnu samācāra]{\kn{ಏನು} \kn{ಸಮಾಚಾರ} (ēnu samācāra) — what's new?}

\label{lesson:KA-C96-whatsnew}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for certainly, then the Kannada for have you eaten.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಏನು} \kn{ಸಮಾಚಾರ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಏನು} \kn{ಸಮಾಚಾರ}?} (\emph{ēnu samācāra?}) — \textquotedblleft{}what's new?\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}what news?\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\kn{ಸಮಾಚಾರ}} (\emph{samācāra}) is \textquotedblleft{}news\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A friendly question after hello.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ēnu samācāra}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ēnu samācāra}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{ēnu samācāra?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for certainly, then the Kannada for have you eaten, then say \emph{ēnu samācāra} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಏನು} \kn{ಸಮಾಚಾರ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}What's new?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[tumbā dina āytu]{\kn{ತುಂಬಾ} \kn{ದಿನ} \kn{ಆಯ್ತು} (tumbā dina āytu) — it's been a long time}

\label{lesson:KA-C96-longtime}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for have you eaten, then the Kannada for what's new.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ತುಂಬಾ} \kn{ದಿನ} \kn{ಆಯ್ತು}}
\textbf{\kn{ತುಂಬಾ} \kn{ದಿನ} \kn{ಆಯ್ತು}} (\emph{tumbā dina āytu}) — \textquotedblleft{}it's been a long time\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}many days have happened\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\kn{ತುಂಬಾ}}, \textquotedblleft{}very, many\textquotedblright{}; \textbf{\kn{ದಿನ}}, \textquotedblleft{}day\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
What you say to a friend you have not seen.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tumbā dina āytu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tumbā dina āytu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{tumbā dina āytu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for have you eaten, then the Kannada for what's new, then say \emph{tumbā dina āytu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ತುಂಬಾ} \kn{ದಿನ} \kn{ಆಯ್ತು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}It's been a long time\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[halō]{\kn{ಹಲೋ} (halō) — hello (on the phone)}

\label{lesson:KA-C96-hello}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for what's new, then the Kannada for long time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಹಲೋ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಹಲೋ}} (\emph{halō}) — \textquotedblleft{}hello\textquotedblright{}, borrowed from English and used above all when answering the phone. Face to face, \textbf{\kn{ನಮಸ್ಕಾರ}} is still the greeting.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The phone's greeting.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{halō}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{halō}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{halō}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for what's new, then the Kannada for long time, then say \emph{halō} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಹಲೋ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Hello (on the phone)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kṣēmavē]{\kn{ಕ್ಷೇಮವೇ} (kṣēmavē) — are you well?}

\label{lesson:KA-C96-wellbeing}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for long time, then the Kannada for hello.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಕ್ಷೇಮವೇ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಕ್ಷೇಮವೇ}?} (\emph{kṣēmavē?}) — \textquotedblleft{}are you well?\textquotedblright{}, a formal, warm question. \textbf{\kn{ಕ್ಷೇಮ}} (\emph{kṣēma}) is \textquotedblleft{}welfare\textquotedblright{}; \textbf{‑\kn{ಏ}} makes it a question.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The formal cousin of hēgiddīrā.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kṣēmavē}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kṣēmavē}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{kṣēmavē?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for long time, then the Kannada for hello, then say \emph{kṣēmavē} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಕ್ಷೇಮವೇ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Are you well?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
